A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhyloLM and provide readable methods, equations, results, figures, tables and appendices. Retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering, and v4 adds Appendices J–K. Localized caption and panel defects do not prevent a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original similarity matrices, phylogenetic reconstructions, benchmark-score predictions, hyperparameter experiments and quantization analyses in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds experiments with alternative prompt sets, prompt lengths and completion lengths in Appendices J–K.

M1.justification: The sampling procedure, four-character completions, Nei similarity and distance, neighbor-joining trees, and ICA plus logistic regression predictor remain unchanged. Appendix C's pseudocode is identical apart from formatting. The added experiments vary inputs and settings without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Appendix J extends the original math/code coverage to Chinese poetry, Wikipedia text and chat-formatted math prompts. These introduce a targeted Chinese-language scenario, general-knowledge text and an interaction-format condition; the original six benchmark-prediction tasks remain.

E2.justification: No competing phylogeny or benchmark-prediction method is added or removed. The known Mistral genealogy remains the reconstruction reference, and Appendix H retains the same GPTQ 4-bit, GPTQ 8-bit and AWQ 4-bit quantization comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include approximately five-character Chinese prompts, an explicit User/Assistant wrapper, prompt-length comparisons at 5, 20–100, 200 and 1000 characters, and completion-length testing from 1–19 characters using off-diagonal RMS contrast. Existing main settings remain. Figures 13–14 also change their captions from leave-one-family-out to leave-one-out, contradicting the retained main-method description; this establishes a reporting change, not that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix J newly tests how language, chat formatting and general-text prompts affect clustering. Appendix K directly examines sensitivity to prompt and completion length, addressing choices previously supported mainly by qualitative reasoning. Earlier sample-count, math/code, mixed-interface and quantization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report eight independent gene sets for the original variability analysis, standard-error bars, correlation tests and the same uncertainty summaries. The new analyses introduce no additional seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval or significance-testing practice. RMS contrast measures matrix variation rather than uncertainty in an estimate.

E6.justification: Appendices J–K add clustering results for Chinese, chat-formatted and Wikipedia prompts, family-clustering results across prompt lengths, and a completion-contrast optimum around 2–4 characters. Existing benchmark tables and plots are retained, including mean correlations of 0.68 ± 0.04 across families and 0.64 ± 0.05 within families. These are additional findings, not improved performance under the original settings.

T1.justification: Appendix K.2 introduces the diagnostic definition of RMS contrast as the standard deviation of off-diagonal similarity entries. Section 2.3 also corrects the index range for eight gene sets from 0–8 to 0–7. The central similarity/distance definitions, variance expressions and phylogenetic assumptions remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central contributions: adapting phylogenetic analysis to LLM outputs, recovering model relationships and predicting benchmark performance efficiently. Additional appendix evidence supports these claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: The new appendices interpret Chinese and chat-prompt clustering in terms of language ability and chat-training familiarity, and use Wikipedia results to support broader prompt applicability. They also recommend short prompts for cost efficiency and short completions for contrast. Existing limitations concerning ancestry, chat interfaces and untested temperature effects remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds explicit code and notebook links on the first page, dataset identifiers and preprocessing instructions for the new prompt sets, and settings for the length experiments. Previously documented hardware, temperature, sampling restrictions and predictor configuration remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the access instructions, not whether the linked resources work.

R1.justification: v4 adds Dawkins's The Selfish Gene to the cultural-evolution motivation and removes several model-source references, including Mixtral, Orca 2 and Zephyr, alongside removing citations from the model tables. The paper's overall positioning around genetic distance, phylogeny and inexpensive LLM evaluation is retained.

P1.justification: v4 rewrites the gene-selection explanation, clarifies four-character retokenization, adds acknowledgments and Appendices J–K, and updates affiliations and citation style. Most main-text prose, section organization and Appendix A–I explanations remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 replaces main Figure 5 with an ARC training/held-out-family illustration and retains the previous summary plot as Appendix Figure 15. Figures 25–32 add substantial matrix, dendrogram and sensitivity displays, alongside conference-template reformatting and figure/table relocation. New presentation defects include Chinese-poetry captions on the figures identified as Wikipedia results in J.3 and an absent matrix in Figure 31(c).

improvement.justification: Appendices J–K provide useful empirical support for previously heuristic prompt and completion choices and broaden checks of applicability; the new code and notebook links also improve reproducibility information. These gains are tempered by inconsistent holdout descriptions, mislabeled Wikipedia figures and the incomplete Figure 31(c). With the central method and benchmark evidence unchanged, the net quality improvement is limited.
